p0.descriptionHtml:
The Raimondi plastic tile beater is the block you tap tiles down with. Lay it flat on the tile and knock it with a rubber mallet, and the whole tile beds into the adhesive at once, which collapses the trowel ridges, fills the back and takes out lippage against the tile next door. Plastic will not warp in a wet van the way a timber block does.

Use it for

  • Bedding floor and wall tiles fully into the adhesive
  • Tapping down high corners to level with neighbouring tiles

Features

  • Plastic construction that won't warp in humidity
  • Grooved flat base stops it suctioning onto the tile
  • Offset handle gives a larger striking surface

Specifications

  • Thickness: 15 mm
  • Material: plastic

Good to know

  • Hit it with Raimondi's white rubber mallet, not a steel hammer, and work from the centre of the tile outwards.
  • For large format and heavy slabs, the rubber faced anti bounce beater or a vibrator does the job with less effort.
  • Wipe adhesive off the base before it dries so it stays flat.

p1.descriptionHtml:
The Raimondi rubber tile beater is a heavy beating block for large format tiles and slabs. Its weight and the anti bounce rubber base push the tile down into the adhesive and drive the air out from underneath, so you get full contact without the block skipping back at you. The white stain free rubber will not mark a polished tile.

Use it for

  • Bedding large format porcelain and slabs into the adhesive
  • Pushing out air pockets under tiles so they do not sound hollow

Features

  • Anti bounce rubber base that protects the tile surface
  • Sturdy galvanised steel frame
  • Offset handle for a larger striking area and less wrist fatigue

Specifications

  • Size: 145 x 350 mm
  • Rubber: white, stain free
  • Weight: about 1.8 kg
  • Model: 142GR

Good to know

  • Work from the centre of the tile out to the edges so trapped air has somewhere to go.
  • Tap it with a rubber mallet or use the weight of the block alone on thin slabs.
  • For whole floors of large format, the Raimondi e-Fox vibrator does the same job faster.

p2.descriptionHtml:
The Raimondi gauging rake spreads self levelling compound to a set depth. Two adjustable pins ride on the floor and hold the blade at the thickness you dial in, so you pull the leveller out to an even 5 or 10 mm across the room instead of guessing by eye and running thin over the high spots. Handle sold separately.

Use it for

  • Spreading self levelling and smoothing compounds to a consistent thickness
  • Spreading fluid screeds and primers over large floors

Specifications

  • Width: 600 mm
  • Depth gauge: 0 to 20 mm, adjustable
  • Takes a Raimondi 27 mm aluminium handle
  • Weight: about 1.6 kg
  • Model: 243

Fits

  • Raimondi 27 mm anodised aluminium handles (133 cm one piece, 133 cm sectional or 178 cm)

Good to know

  • Raimondi sells spare tempered pins (4 mm x 60 mm, kit of 24, Art. 243PE01A) for when the originals wear.
  • Rinse the rake straight after the pour. Set leveller will not come off the blade.
  • Follow up with spiked shoes and a spiked roller if the product calls for it.

p3.descriptionHtml:
The Raimondi white rubber mallet is the tiler's mallet for tapping tiles down and knocking a beating block. The white rubber is non marking, so it leaves no black smudges on a pale tile, and it is anti bounce, so the energy goes into the tile rather than back up your arm. Choose 500 g for wall tiles or 1 kg for floors and slabs.

Use it for

  • Tapping tiles down into the adhesive
  • Striking a tile beater or beating block
  • Seating levelling wedges and trims

Features

  • Non marking white rubber head
  • Anti bounce rubber
  • Head moulded in one piece around a reinforced steel core handle, so it will not fly off
  • Balanced to reduce strain on the wrist

Specifications

  • 500 g: Raimondi Art. 176500BC
  • 1000 g: Raimondi Art. 1761KGBC

Good to know

  • Wipe adhesive off the head before it sets or it will mark the next tile.
  • Tap glazed and polished tiles through a beating block rather than directly.

p4.descriptionHtml:
The Raimondi Iperbet is a bucket mixer for tile adhesive, thinset, plaster mortar, quartz plaster and concrete. Instead of a paddle spinning in a bucket, the 45 litre bucket turns against a fixed mixing tool at low speed, so the mix does not trap air and comes out even every time. It mixes about 300 kg an hour, and with two buckets supplied you tip one out while the next batch is going.

Use it for

  • Mixing bagged tile adhesive and thinset on big floors

Features

  • Rotating 45 L bucket on wheeled legs
  • Fixed mixing tool: safer for the operator and lets you watch the mix as it goes
  • Double blade mixing tool
  • Mixes at low RPM to avoid trapping air, for a smooth, even mix

Specifications

  • Bucket: 45 litres, two supplied
  • Output: about 300 kg per hour
  • Size: 60 x 51 x 77 cm, about 34 kg
  • Single phase 230 V
  • Made in Italy

What's in the box

  • Two 45 L buckets, standard mixing blade, hex key and manual

Good to know

  • The clump breaker and fluid mixing kit are add ons for powdery adhesive and for grout and self leveller.

p5.descriptionHtml:
Replacement three spiral mixing paddle for the Raimondi Fluid Mix and Fluid Mix Special stations. The extended 680 mm shaft reaches the bottom of the 75 litre bucket, and the 140 mm three spiral head is shaped for runny products, so self leveller and grout come out lump free without whipping air into them. The M14 thread also fits hand mixers.

Fits

  • Raimondi Fluid Mix Special and Fluid Mix (the stirrer supplied with them)
  • BAT Pro and other M14 thread hand mixers

Specifications

  • Head diameter: 140 mm
  • Length: 680 mm
  • Thread: M14
  • Three spiral paddle, galvanised steel
  • Raimondi lists the Fluid Mix stirrer as Art. 178 389H

Use it for

  • Self levelling compounds, premixed products, cement based grout and paint

Good to know

  • Mix at low speed for fluid products. High speed drags air in and leaves pinholes in the leveller.
  • Rinse the paddle straight after mixing so leveller does not set on the spirals.
  • For stiff adhesive use a double spiral or four blade paddle instead.

p6.descriptionHtml:
Raimondi small spiral mixing paddle with an M14 thread for hand mixers. The spiral lifts material from the bottom of the bucket as it turns, so grout, self leveller and paint mix through without air, and the smaller head suits 10 to 20 litre buckets where a big paddle would throw product up the sides.

Fits

  • BAT Pro 1050 W and 1600 W hand mixers
  • Any other M14 thread drill mixer

Use it for

  • Grout, self leveller, primers and paint in smaller buckets
  • Small batches of fluid compound and premixed products

Specifications

  • Thread: M14
  • Reinforced double spiral, galvanised steel

Good to know

  • Raimondi makes its double spiral paddles in 120, 140 and 160 mm heads. This is the small one; the large spiral and 160 x 600 mm paddles are listed separately for bigger buckets.
  • Run the mixer at low speed for fluid products so you do not whip air in.
  • Rinse the spiral straight after mixing. Set grout is hard to get out of the coils.

p7.descriptionHtml:
Raimondi large spiral mixing paddle with an M14 thread for hand mixers. The bigger spiral head moves more material per turn, so a full bag of self leveller or a 20 litre bucket of grout mixes through quickly and evenly, lifting the powder off the bottom instead of leaving a dry layer under the paddle.

Fits

  • BAT Pro 1050 W and 1600 W hand mixers
  • Any other M14 thread drill mixer

Use it for

  • Larger batches of self leveller, grout and paint
  • Fluid compounds and premixed products in 20 to 30 litre buckets

Specifications

  • Thread: M14
  • Reinforced double spiral, galvanised steel

Good to know

  • Match the paddle to the mixer. A large spiral in heavy material loads up a small mixer, so use it with the 1600 W BAT Pro or similar for big batches.
  • Raimondi also lists a 160 mm head on a 600 mm shaft for deep buckets.
  • Rinse the spiral straight after mixing.
